cases.note: The root form: each row belongs to one account, recorded in `accountId`, which the engine fills in at write time.
A row that takes the account of the row a field names. The field's own @relationship says which concept that is, so the declaration names only the field.

The same, where the field holds a bare id and carries no @relationship: parent= writes out the concept, by its canonical id, and it has to be a registered one (negative/concept/belongs-to-parent-unknown.memql).
A concept holding cluster-provided rows beside its accounts' rows. On it a row with no account is a statement rather than a gap.

The concept's own writers state the account, so the engine never fills the field and never refuses a change to it. The field is still required: every reader of the declaration reads `accountId`, whoever wrote it.
Cluster-wide: never inside an account, and no `accountId` field is asked for.

cases.message: @belongsTo on a concept takes keyword arguments
@belongsTo on a concept has no key acount -- did you mean account?
@belongsTo is written more than once on a concept
cases.note: One concept, one answer. The annotation registry's repeat rule refuses the second declaration before either is read for what it means, so this carries the registry's code rather than belongs_to_conflict.

cases.message: @belongsTo(account, cluster) names both -- a concept's rows belong to an account or are cluster-wide, never both
`stated` leaves the account to the concept's own writers, and `via` has the engine take it from a parent
cases.note: `stated` and `via` are two answers to who decides the account. A row that follows a parent is engine-managed by definition.

cases.message: records the account in a field named `accountId`, and the concept declares none
cases.note: The field's name is fixed so a reader of whose-row-is-this needs no per-concept knowledge, which only holds if every account-scoped concept declares it.

cases.message: records the account in `accountId`, which the concept declares as []string
cases.note: One row belongs to one account. A concept that also takes a list of accounts keeps the list in a field of its own beside the single one.

cases.message: names a field the concept does not declare
cases.note: A via naming no field resolves to no parent on every write, and the write does not fail: the row falls through to the call's account and is filed under the wrong one.

cases.message: The account grant opens a row to the members of the account
cases.note: @rowAuthz(account=...) puts a concept's rows inside accounts; declaring it cluster-wide says they are inside none, and the row gate and the inventory would then disagree about the same row.

A kind whose rows belong to an account and never leave this cluster. `stays` names one of three reasons -- signin, transit or machine -- which an account export prints beside the count it leaves behind.
`stays` sits beside any account form, a `via` included. A kind that stays may follow a kind that travels; the reverse is refused at load (negative/concept/belongs-to-via-stays.memql).
A cluster-wide kind is in no account, so no account export reads it and there is nothing for it to stay out of.

cases.message: gives no reason the kind stays -- write stays= with one of signin, transit or machine
cases.note: The reasons are a closed list because a file's report prints them: an open value would let a misspelling stand as a fourth reason nobody explains.
